$comment: The pre-alert board as a process owner leaves it once a review has finished
with it. The incomplete one beside this file is where it starts.
Same name as the first draft, deliberately: it is the same process at a
later stage, and the board's name becomes the agent's directory. A fixture
label in there would name the generated code after the fixture.
The pair is what makes the reviewer measurable, and neither number means
anything without a board somebody would actually call done:
ablate one fact from this   a working reviewer asks for it back   7/7
run it untouched            a finished board should stay quiet    0 blanks
What review added, over the first draft:
· recipients on the COA report        the SOP never said who receives it
· a system on the invoice report      'log an error' never said where
· an idempotency key on both          a resumed shipment reported twice
· on_missing_input on both checks     what to do while still waiting
· an edge for mismatched_coa          the SOP named the outcome, not the path
· e7 and e8, the way back             failure was drawn as final; it is not
Both reports lead back rather than ending, which is the answer to the one
question that unlocks the second half of this process: a discrepancy is
reported and the shipment returns once the paperwork is fixed.
Still not answered here, because a drawing cannot say it: what counts as the
same batch number, which certificate wins when two could match, how long the
wait is. Those are statements, and they live in the spec.

config.name: Pre-alert email
config.identified_by: it arrives in the pre-alert group mailbox the bot has access to
config.instructions: The SOP says documentation must be reported by email but never says to whom. The sender is the obvious candidate and is deliberately not assumed here. One email carries a subject and a list of attachments, and the attachments are what there are several of; that a shipment gets several emails over days is a fact about the trigger rather than about what an email is.

config.name: Commercial Invoice
config.instructions: The invoice number is in the top-right corner.

config.name: Certificate of Analysis
config.identified_by: the page header reads "Certificate of Analysis"

config.name: Shipment summary
config.instructions: One row per shipment, which is the thing this process exists to produce. Nothing recognises it and nothing counts it, because it never arrives — the checks write into it as they run and it is what the process hands back. Seven fields, one per check measurement. The historical report carries two more, an ASN mismatch count and an open/closed status, and neither is here because nothing on this board can produce either: no card reads an ASN, and no card decides what closes a shipment. Declaring a column the process cannot fill would make the board claim something untrue, so the gap belongs in the review rather than in this list.

config.name: Pre-alert documents received
config.match_condition: subject contains "Pre-Alert Documents" or "APL USA // PRE-ALERT DOCUMENTATION"
config.instructions: Sent by the exporter's clearing agent. Documents arrive in pieces — a shipment may get several emails, and corrected COAs come days later.

config.name: Does every line item include HTS, FDA product code, NDC and ANDA?
config.instructions: Review the "Description of Goods" section and make sure every line item carries all four identifiers.

config.name: Log the invoice error
config.instructions: Log an error naming the invoice number, the drug description and which information type is missing.

config.name: Does every batch on the invoice have a matching COA?

outcomes.name: missing_coa
outcomes.description: a batch on the invoice has no COA

outcomes.name: mismatched_coa
outcomes.description: a COA exists but its batch number disagrees

config.instructions: Each batch should have its own COA. Cross-check each batch listed on the invoice against a corresponding COA document.

config.name: Report the COA discrepancy
config.instructions: Report missing or mismatched COAs by email with the invoice number, the batch numbers and a description of the discrepancy.
